name: Triangle-AABB Intersection (Separating Axis Theorem)
definition: An algorithm to determine if a triangle intersects an Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) by projecting both shapes onto 9 potential separating axes: 3 face normals of the AABB and 6 cross products of triangle edges and AABB axes.
summary: Triangle-AABB Intersection uses the Separating Axis Theorem to determine overlap by testing 13 potential separating axes, distinguishing it from simpler bounding box checks.
